- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is high (e.g., >0.7) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (e.g., <0.3) — model is overly optimistic or fails to reflect bearish signals.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays reacting to recent price drops or sentiment shifts — adjust forecast by 1–2 periods backward for mean reversion signals.
- When sentiment is rising sharply, model overreacts with upward bias — reduce forecast slope or apply dampening factor.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts mid-term price peaks — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 14-day high.
- If sentiment is volatile (rapid swings), model fails to smooth — apply moving average filter or sentiment-weighted smoothing.
- When sentiment is neutral or flat, model tends to drift — anchor forecast to recent 7-day average unless sentiment shifts.
- Avoid forecasting sharp reversals without sentiment confirmation — require sentiment >0.6 for reversal predictions.
